title: The SUMIF function: adding up with a condition
summary: SUMIF adds up the values whose matching cells meet one condition, such as the sales of one region.
intro: `SUMIF` checks the condition in one range and adds up the matching values from another range. The condition can be text, a number, a comparison such as `">100"`, or a reference to a cell.
args: The range where the condition is checked.
The condition: text in quotation marks, a number, a comparison or a reference.
The values to add. If you leave it out, the first range itself is added.
examples: Total sales of the North region: 120, 40 and 60.
Total of the sales that are 90 or more.
errors: On this site, the condition range and the range to add have different sizes.

faq.q: How do I add up with more than one condition?
faq.a: Use `SUMIFS`, where the range to add comes first.

faq.q: Does the condition tell upper case from lower case?
faq.a: No, matching does not distinguish them.
